authorities.name: Criminal Justice Act 2003, s.114
authorities.date_note: Enactment year. The text verified this session is the current in-force version, but legislation.gov.uk's own page flags pending future amendments (from Acts cited there as '2026 c. 2' and '2026 c. 20') not yet in force as of this file's verification date - neither affects the substantive text of s.114(1) quoted here, confirmed live this session.
authorities.proposition: In criminal proceedings, an out-of-court statement (hearsay) is admissible for the truth of its contents only if: (a) a statutory provision in this Chapter or elsewhere makes it admissible, (b) a preserved common-law exception under s.118 applies, (c) all parties agree, or (d) the court is satisfied it is in the interests of justice to admit it - guided by the nine non-exhaustive factors in s.114(2) (probative value, other available evidence, importance to the case, reliability of the maker and of the account of the statement's making, difficulty of challenge, and resulting prejudice).
authorities.verification_note: Fetched live and directly this session.

authorities.name: R v Horncastle and others
authorities.proposition: A conviction based solely or decisively on hearsay evidence admitted under the CJA 2003 gateways (including the s.114(1)(d) interests-of-justice gateway) does not automatically breach Article 6(3)(d) ECHR. The Court declined to import the Strasbourg 'sole or decisive rule' (that a conviction may never rest solely or decisively on the untested evidence of an absent witness) as a rigid domestic requirement, holding that Parliament's CJA 2003 statutory safeguards (the s.114(2) factors, s.125's stopping power, s.126's additional exclusionary discretion, and PACE 1984 s.78) render that rule unnecessary in the English system, and that the later Strasbourg decision in Al-Khawaja does not establish otherwise.

what_this_is_not: Two verified nodes covering the general hearsay-admissibility framework and its Article 6 compatibility. Does not cover the specific statutory hearsay exceptions (business/other documents under ss.117, 116), the preserved common-law exceptions (s.118), disclosure duties under the Criminal Procedure and Investigations Act 1996, PACE 1984's own exclusionary discretion (s.78) in detail, bad character evidence, or any other Criminal Procedure & Evidence subject - all remain unbuilt.
